lesson.text: Quick memory: a square has 4 equal sides and a triangle has 3 sides. Today we look closer: at corners, angles and lines.
A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book. A square and a rectangle have 4 right angles. We mark a right angle with a little square.
An angle smaller than a right angle is acute. One bigger than a right angle, but smaller than a straight line, is obtuse. Hold a book's corner against an angle to check.
Parallel lines never meet, like the rails of a track. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Other lines that cross are intersecting.
A quadrilateral has 4 sides. A rectangle has 4 right angles. A square has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. A rhombus has 4 equal sides, but its corners are not square.
Triangles by their sides: an equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, an isosceles triangle 2 and a scalene triangle none. A right-angled triangle has one right angle.
Split a shape into equal parts: this hexagon is cut into 6 equal triangles, so each one is 1/6 of it. Next, in grade 4: angles in degrees and lines of symmetry.

exercises.hint: Count the sides. Are they all the same length?
exercises.explain: It has 4 right angles, and its long sides are longer than its short sides: a rectangle.

exercises.prompt: How many right angles does a square have?
exercises.hint: Every corner of a square is a square corner.

exercises.prompt: What kind of lines are these?
exercises.explain: They never meet, however far they go: parallel lines.

exercises.prompt: This angle is a right angle.
exercises.explain: Yes: it is a square corner, marked with a little square.

exercises.prompt: Which is true? This angle is …
exercises.hint: Hold the corner of a book against it.
exercises.explain: It is narrower than a square corner: smaller than a right angle.

exercises.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?

exercises.hint: 4 equal sides, but are the corners square?
exercises.explain: 4 equal sides and no right angles: a rhombus.

exercises.prompt: What kind of lines are these?
exercises.hint: Do they meet at a square corner?
exercises.explain: They meet at a right angle: perpendicular lines.

exercises.prompt: The shape is cut into equal parts. What fraction of the whole shape is the shaded part?
A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides.
exercises.explain: Yes: the top and bottom are parallel, and so are the two sides.

exercises.hint: Do a rectangle's sides all have to be the same length?
exercises.explain: No: a rectangle's long sides can be longer than its short sides.

exercises.prompt: What kind of angle is this?
exercises.hint: Is it wider than a square corner?
exercises.explain: It is wider than a right angle: an obtuse angle.

exercises.prompt: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. What is it called?
exercises.hint: How many sides are the same length?
exercises.explain: All 3 sides are equal: an equilateral triangle.

exercises.prompt: Which shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles?
exercises.hint: A square has right angles. Which shape does not?
exercises.explain: A rhombus has 4 equal sides and no right angles.

exercises.prompt: How many right angles does this shape have inside it?
exercises.explain: A right-angled triangle has 1 right angle.

exercises.prompt: A square is a special rhombus.
exercises.hint: Does a square have 4 equal sides?
exercises.explain: Yes: a square has 4 equal sides like a rhombus, and right angles too.

exercises.prompt: Which shape is cut into equal parts?
exercises.hint: Equal parts are all the same size.
exercises.explain: The square's 4 triangles are all the same size.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, smallest first.
exercises.hint: A right angle is a square corner; a straight line is two right angles.
exercises.explain: Acute is smaller than a right angle, obtuse is bigger, and a straight line is bigger still.

exercises.prompt: A rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts. What fraction of it is each part?
